---
title: "STACK compliance"
subtitle: "Expected behavior, engine agreement, and known limitations"
---

Each case asks whether a particular STACK answer test accepts a submitted answer. This report shows which cases STACK SymPy can check, where its result agrees with STACK, and where a teacher should expect a difference.

**Port** means STACK SymPy. **STACK** means the reference Moodle/Maxima answer test. **Expected** is the outcome recorded in the original test case. A matching outcome for one case is useful evidence, but it does not prove that every question using that answer test will behave identically.

[Semantics and open questions](semantics.qmd) explains the assumptions behind the cases where results differ, including domain restrictions and identities that the port cannot prove.

  <span class="tone-bad">Red: unexpected result</span>

</div>

<details class="methodology">
<summary>Scope and technical details</summary>

This compares CAS answer-test functions rather than complete Moodle grading sessions. The port currently provides ten native-compatible answer-test families, including bounded nested scalar lists/sets with `AlgEquiv`, `Sets`, `SameType` and `EqualComAss`, and bounded matrices with `AlgEquiv`, `SameType` and `EqualComAss`. Cases outside port coverage stay in the inventory and are labeled by the missing answer test or unsupported input/feature. Some direct reference calls are also omitted because they need parser or controller preparation.

“Test applicability” asks whether an answer test can compare the supplied values. It is separate from input syntax validity and from the final accept/reject mark. Form tests such as `EqualComAss` can reject mathematically equivalent expressions.

Source codes `0` and `1` mean expected rejection and acceptance; `-1` expects a controlled error. Codes `-2` and `-3` flag source-authored native deviations. Only specifically reviewed cases are labeled “Known STACK issue.” Ordinary feedback notes are retained but not generally compared; asserted controlled-error notes are checked separately.

The Python-only `IsBasis`, `MatrixProperty` and `PythonChecker` tests are documented in
[Python answer tests](../docs/python-checker-api.html). Their example, unit
and browser checks are separate from this native report; they do not enlarge
the 2,303-row inventory or its native coverage counts.

Browser agreement includes input/scope classifications as well as graded results. The summary separates these. STACK coverage counts available observations, not compatibility passes.
